Why go: a big, well-equipped speedboat for fishing or Koh Phangan

Sting is a 36 ft Gulf Craft built to US Coast Guard standards, with twin outboards that cruise at about 30 knots, full shade, a toilet, a swim-platform shower and a fridge. It also carries Garmin navigation, radar, sonar and a fish finder, which is why it doubles as one of the better-equipped fishing boats on the north coast.

On the Koh Phangan day the speed means more time at the beaches; on the fishing day it means reaching productive water quickly and moving if the fish aren't biting.

The fishing day in detail

After pickup at 08:30 and a safety briefing, the boat leaves Bang Rak at 09:15 and starts trolling for king mackerel and barracuda from about 10:00. After a lunch break at a beach restaurant (own cost), the afternoon is bottom fishing for snapper, grouper and trevally, with a swimming stop in a quiet cove. You are back at the pier around 16:30. The crew sets up rods, bait and tackle and shows beginners how to fish, so you don't need experience.

Who it suits

  • Groups of 6–10 who want comfort and speed.
  • Anglers, from beginners to experienced, who want proper gear.
  • Guests staying in Bophut, Choeng Mon or Chaweng, where transfer is included.

Who should choose something else

  • Small groups on a budget: the Kamonwan costs less for up to 5.
  • Anyone wanting a relaxed sail: try a catamaran charter.

Good to know

  • On request: the boat is not on a fixed schedule; we confirm your date by email or WhatsApp after booking, and refund in full if it isn't available.
  • Catch: fish are never guaranteed; the crew moves spots using the sonar, but quiet days happen.
  • Booking: online booking for tomorrow closes at midnight Thai time.
